sentences.text:
Petitioners are seeking to quash the FIR in Crime No.14/2024 registered at Whitefield Women Police Station, Bengaluru City and the consequential proceedings pending on the file of the XXIX Additional CJM, Bengaluru in C.C.No.76048/2024.
2.

entities.text: Whitefield Women Police Station, Bengaluru City
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute, wherein respondent No.2 has set the law in motion, consequent to which, the proceedings are initiated against the petitioners for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
3.
The petitioners and respondent No.2 are present before the Court.

It is submitted that the dispute has been amicably settled and joint petition was filed under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act,
1955, before the Family Court, Tiruvallur, seeking dissolution of the marriage by mutual consent.

Before this Court, a petition is filed under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking permission to permit the parties to compound the case NC:
2025:KHC:49674 HC-KAR and to quash the entire proceedings.
The said petition is supported by the affidavits of petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2.

4. The respondent No.2/defacto complainant is present before the Court and submits that she has given her voluntary consent to withdraw the case and she has no objection if the criminal proceedings pending against the petitioners are quashed.
5. The petition and the affidavits of the parties are placed on record.

6. A memo is filed by the learned counsel for the petitioners stating that in light of the amicable settlement arrived at between the parties, petitioner No.1 has paid an amount of Rs.4,50,000/-
towards full and final settlement to respondent No.2 by way of Demand Draft bearing No.685229 for Rs.2,50,000/- and Demand Draft bearing No.685671 for Rs.2,00,000/- respectively drawn on State Bank of India, Gandhi Nagar, Tiruvannamalai Branch, in addition to NC: 2025:KHC:49674 HC-KAR Rs.3,00,000/- already paid to respondent No.2 before the Family Court, Tiruvallur.
Memo is placed on record.
7. Receipt of the demand drafts is acknowledged by respondent No.2 and the learned counsel.

8. Considering that the matter arises out of matrimonial dispute and since the parties have entered into an amicable settlement and respondent No.2 having expressed no objection for quashing the proceedings pending against the petitioners, to secure the ends of justice, it is expedient to allow the petition and quash the proceedings, as continuation of proceedings would serve no useful purpose.
